findings.title: Denial cache key uses raw UserUID instead of resolved UID and omits IdentityType
findings.body: `Check` constructs `permDenialKey` directly from `checkReq.UserUID` (the raw ID from the request subject) without including `checkReq.IdentityType` or resolving user identifiers via `GetUserIdentifiers` (unlike `permCache`, which resolves numeric IDs to `userIdentifiers.UID` and separates anonymous permissions). This has two consequences: (1) different identity types with the same ID (e.g., `anonymous:0` vs `user:0` or `service-account:1` vs `user:1`) share the same denial cache key, so a denial for an anonymous request can falsely deny a user or service account with the same numeric ID; and (2) a user checked by numeric ID (`user:123`) and by UID (`user:uid123`) will use two different denial cache keys instead of sharing the entry.

findings.title: Stale folderCache prevents inheriting permissions on newly created nested folders/dashboards
findings.body: When `Check` falls back to `getIdentityPermissions` on a permission cache miss (lines 139-146), it refreshes `permCache` from the database, but `checkInheritedPermissions` still calls `buildFolderTree`, which reads from `s.folderCache` without invalidating or bypassing it. If a user creates a subfolder `child` inside a `parent` folder where they have permissions, and then creates or accesses a resource inside `child` while `folderCache` still holds the pre-creation folder tree (cached for `shortCacheTTL`), `tree.Ancestors("child")` will return no ancestors, `checkPermission` will return `false`, and `s.permDenialCache.Set` (line 154) will cache the false denial for 30 seconds.

findings.title: Test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' sets permCache to false instead of true
findings.body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ('Should deny on explicit cache deny entry'), the comment on line 981 says `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`, but line 982 sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` instead of `true`. Even if `permDenialCache` were completely ignored, `checkPermission` would still return `false` (and `fakeStore` has no permissions either), so the test does not actually verify that `permDenialCache` short-circuits `permCache`.
